note: docs/internal/voice-naturalness.md (home-legacy): a robot says 'The current time is 9:51 PM', a person says 'it's 9:51'. The canonical example this step names.

utterance: is it going to rain today
robotic: The answer to your question is yes, it is going to rain today.
note: elliptical answers piggyback the question's frame ('What time is it?' gets 'Five o'clock.', never a restated full sentence).

robotic: Your grocery list contains the following items: milk, eggs, and bread.
natural: You've got milk, eggs, and bread.
note: a list spoken as a sentence, not read back with framing language or bullet punctuation.
rounding is the default, precision is marked: exact numbers only where exactness is the point (an appointment time, a corrected fact).

utterance: what's the weather going to be like tomorrow
robotic: It will be sunny and 72 degrees tomorrow.
natural: Supposed to be sunny, around seventy.
note: a forecast is never asserted as flat fact - real speakers hedge secondhand information with an evidential every time.

utterance: the dog's name is Rex, right
robotic: No, that is incorrect. The dog's name is actually Riff, not Rex.
note: factual correction is flat and instant (just the corrected value), unlike opinion disagreement, which is delayed and softened.

robotic: You're very welcome! I'm happy to help with anything else you might need.
note: acknowledgment tokens are tiny and varied (Sure. / Mhm. / Okay.), never 'Certainly!' or a restatement of the request.

utterance: why did the router just restart
robotic: I do not have enough information to determine the exact cause of the router restart at this time.
robotic_re: (?i)i do not have enough information|at this time
note: 'I don't know' is a real answer, under five words, unapologetic - not a hedge about the limits of the assistant's knowledge.
